summary: The Django User.note attribute is renamed to customer_note while keeping db_column='note', so the database column note remains unchanged. Both the old and new versions write to the same column note; the old via the note attribute, the new via customer_note resolved to note by Django. With no column rename, no SQL data migration is needed. Deploy the new version with its migration applied, then retire the old version.
write_consistency: Both versions write to the identical database column note: the old version includes note in its INSERT/UPDATE statements via its known model attribute, and the new version includes note via customer_note with db_column='note'. Reads through the GraphQL field note return the most recent value written by either version, preserving consistency during the concurrent overlap.
revision_notes: Renamed Django attribute User.note to customer_note with db_column='note'; new app version code already maps the attribute and GraphQL field; no SQL stages required because the database column name does not change.
